messages:
sophia: Heads-up — FinStream (enterprise) asked for a per-org routing override so all requests with their org header hit Dedicated (low-latency GPUs). They want header-based allowlist + an expiry (30d), and an audit trail. Plz advise on risk + UX.

liam: Question: do they want EVERY route forced to Dedicated or just generation/chat endpoints?

sophia: generation/chat only (text-generation + chat). embeddings/rerank unaffected.

andrew: We have existing per-tenant routing ACLs but they're pretty coarse. Two immediate concerns: precedence vs. org header routing, and what if Dedicated pool saturates? We need automatic fallback policy.

maya: +1 to fallback. Recommend: rule with explicit priority and a fallback param like "fallback: hosted:compat-model". Also need quota accounting so they still get billed properly.

rachel: UX notes: console should let us create a temporary override (start, expiry) and show a diff of routing rules that will apply. Ops need a one-click rollback.

liam: config sketch (for infra/eng):
```yaml
rules:
  - id: finstream-org-override
    match:
      header: "X-Redwood-Org"
      value: "finstream"
    apply:
      route_to: dedicated:pool-lowlatency
      endpoints: ["/v1/generate","/v1/chat/completions"]
    priority: 100
    expiry: 2025-11-30T23:59:59Z
    fallback: hosted:fast-compat
```

andrew: That looks good. Couple of clarifications: priority 100 should beat route-based host rules. We need rule evaluation docs: header overrides > route match > default strategy. Also enforce a max expiry (90d) unless enterprise contract signed.

security-bot: NOTE: Any header-based override must be tied to org-auth (signed JWT or SAML assertion). Plain header matching is vulnerable to spoofing from misconfigured proxies. Recommend require signed header or mTLS.

rachel: Console UX: add a toggle "Require signed assertion" when creating override. If disabled, show a red warning and require owner ack.

maya: Telemetry: we must tag all requests that matched the override with metadata (rule_id) so billing, latency dashboards, and regression alerts can slice by override. Also track failed fallbacks (requests routed to hosted due to capacity) for SLA reports.

liam: Implementation notes: runtime already supports per-route metadata. We'll add a per-request header injection: X-RW-Route-Override: finstream-org-override and emit a policy.audit event to event-log.

andrew: Ops — we should throttle overrides that would move >30% of Dedicated pool to a single org, unless we get explicit capacity reservation. Otherwise risk noisy neighbor.

sophia: FinStream claims they can take a small reserved slot. I'll loop in sales/legal for contract + capacity commit.

rachel: Action items: 1) eng-platform to spec evaluation order + fallback behavior (liam/andrew) 2) eng-runtime to add rule tags + fallback metrics (maya) 3) console to prototype create/edit UI with expiry & signed-assertion toggle (rachel) 4) security to define required auth for header overrides (security-bot) 5) PM (sophia) to coordinate customer contract + capacity.

andrew: I'll open a short RFC and include the YAML sample + precedence table. Will request a review by EOD.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/override-audit (CI passed) — staging rollout scheduled at 2025-10-04T02:00:00Z :rocket:

rachel: Thanks — can we add an audit trail UI element to the rule detail page showing policy changes and who ack'd them?

maya: +1. Also add a small Eval harness to run a few sample prompts through Dedicated vs Hosted to validate output parity (client may want quality guarantees).

sophia: Great, thanks everyone. I'll keep FinStream in the loop and share the RFC once andrew posts it. :thumbsup:
